raw_text:
Here is a comprehensive 12-week strength + hypertrophy program for a 26-year-old recreational lifter with no cycle-related contraindications, starting 2026-06-01. It emphasizes progressive overload for strength and hypertrophy, with body composition improvements in mind. The plan includes weekly structure, sessions, exercises, sets/reps, progression cues, and recovery/nutrition notes. Adjustments can be made based on equipment and client response.

Overall structure
- Training frequency: 4 days per week (e.g., Mon/Tue off Wed/Thu Fri/Sat or similar, with at least 48 hours between lower-body/upper-body sessions when possible).
- Phases: 4 phases of 3 weeks each, plus a deload week at the end of Phase 4 (Week 12) if planned, or you can position the deload in Week 11–12 depending on fatigue.
- Focus each phase:
  - Phase 1 (Weeks 1–3): Foundation strength and hypertrophy, technique emphasis, establishing baselines, RPE 7–8 in main lifts.
  - Phase 2 (Weeks 4–6): Increase intensity, volume tailored for hypertrophy and strength (lower rep ranges with progressive overload).
  - Phase 3 (Weeks 7–9): Strength emphasis with higher loads, maintain hypertrophy with varied rep schemes, introduce some strength-specific accessories.
  - Phase 4 (Weeks 10–12): Peak strength and refinement, final deload or taper depending on response; if peaking, Week 12 can be lighter to taper.
- Daily structure: 
  - 5–10 min warm-up (dynamic) + mobility
  - 4–5 main lifts per session (2–3 compound + 1–2 accessories)
  - Core and accessory work after main lifts
  - 5–10 min cooling/stretching

Weekly plan outline (example: Monday/Tuesday/Thursday/Friday)
- Upper-Lower split with optional push/pull emphasis as fits client
- Each session includes main lower/upper lifts with progression targets
- Accessibility: include alternative exercises if equipment limited (e.g., switch to goblet squats if barbell back squats unavailable)

Phase 1: Foundation & technique (Weeks 1–3)
Goals: establish technique, baseline strength, and muscular endurance; build a solid base for progressive overload.
Weeks 1–3 Session structure (example)

Week 1 (Base, RPE 7–8)
- Day A (Lower)
  - Squat (Back or Front): 3 sets × 5 reps at RPE 7–8
  - Romanian Deadlift: 3 × 8
  - Leg Press or DB Bulgarian Split Squat: 3 × 10
  - Glute Ham Raise or Supine Hamstring Curl: 3 × 10
  - Calf raises: 3 × 12–15
  - Core: Plank 3 × 45 sec
- Day B (Upper)
  - Bench Press or DB Press: 3 × 5
  - Bent-Over Row or T-Bar Row: 3 × 8
  - Overhead Press: 3 × 8
  - Lat Pulldown or Pull-ups (assisted if needed): 3 × 8–10
  - DB Fly or Chest Supported Row: 3 × 12
  - Tricep pushdown: 3 × 12
  - Core: Dead Bug 3 × 12
- Day C (Lower) similar to Day A but varying accessory selection
- Day D (Upper) similar to Day B with slight variation

Weeks 2–3
- Increase volume slightly or weight by 2.5–5% where form remains solid
- Maintain 5s reps for main lifts or shift to 3 × 5 + 2 × 8 where appropriate
- Add optional tempo work (e.g., 2–0–2 tempo on squat)

Phase 2: Hypertrophy-focused with strength reinforcement (Weeks 4–6)
Goals: higher training density, improved muscle size and continuing strength gains.
Weeks 4–6 Session structure

Week 4 (Hypertrophy emphasis)
- Day A (Lower)
  - Squat: 4 × 6 (moderate weight, RPE 8)
  - Romanian Deadlift: 3 × 8
  - Leg Press: 3 × 12
  - Bulgarian Split Squat: 3 × 10 per leg
  - Calf raises: 4 × 12
  - Core: Farmer’s carries 3 × 30 sec
- Day B (Upper)
  - Bench Press: 4 × 6
  - Bent-Over Row: 3 × 8
  - Overhead Press: 3 × 8
  - Pull-Ups/Lat Pulldown: 3 × 8–10
  - Chest Fly or Pec Deck: 3 × 12
  - Tricep Drench: 3 × 12
  - Core: Pallof press 3 × 12 per side
- Day C (Lower)
  - Front Squat or Back Squat: 4 × 5–6
  - Romanian Deadlift or Stiff-Legged: 3 × 8
  - Smith Machine glute hinge or Hip Thrust: 3 × 10
  - Hamstring Curl: 3 × 12
  - Calf: 4 × 12
- Day D (Upper)
  - Incline Dumbbell Press: 4 × 8
  - Seated Cable Row: 3 × 8
  - Lateral Raises: 3 × 12
  - Face Pulls: 3 × 15
  - Bicep Curls: 3 × 12
  - Core: Bike 3 × 1 min

Weeks 5–6
- Increase intensity on main lifts to 3–4% higher or add one additional set while keeping reps steady
- Keep accessory volume similar
- Introduce time-under-tension cues: 2–0–2 on primary lifts to target hypertrophy
- Optional drop sets on the last set of a key exercise if form remains solid

Phase 3: Strength emphasis with hypertrophy maintenance (Weeks 7–9)
Goals: move heavier weights, maintain muscle mass, reduce fatigue
Weeks 7–9 Session structure

Week 7
- Day A (Lower Heavy)
  - Squat: 4 × 4–5 (heavy, RPE 8–9)
  - Deadlift (sumo or conventional or RDL alternative): 3 × 5
  - Leg Press or Hack Squat: 3 × 8
  - Glute/Ham Raises: 3 × 8
  - Calf: 4 × 10
- Day B (Upper Heavy)
  - Bench Press: 4 × 4–5
  - Barbell Row: 4 × 6
  - Overhead Press: 3 × 6
  - Weighted Chin-Ups: 3 × 6–8
  - Dips or Close-Grip Press: 3 × 8
  - Core: Ab wheel or hanging leg raises 3 × 10

Week 8
- Similar to Week 7 but adjust weights to hit RPE 8–9, maintain technique
- Add short deload on accessory work if needed to manage fatigue

Week 9
- 4 × 3–5 on main lifts, with 2–3 accessory moves at 8–10 reps
- Emphasize grip, core stability, and posture

Phase 4: Peaking, energy balance, and generalization (Weeks 10–12)
Goals: peak strength, refine technique, adjust body composition with controlled volume
Weeks 10–11
- Day A (Lower)
  - Squat: 5 × 3–4 heavy (RPE 9)
  - Deadlift or Hip Hinges: 3 × 3–5
  - Lateral Squat Variations or Lunges: 3 × 6–8
  - Glute/Ham Raise: 3 × 6–8
  - Calf: 4 × 8–12
- Day B (Upper)
  - Bench Press: 5 × 3–4
  - Weighted Pull-Ups/Chin-Ups: 4 × 4–6
  - Overhead Press: 3 × 5
  - Row Variation: 3 × 6–8
  - Dips/Push-Ups: 3 × 8–12
  - Core: Plank variations 3 × 60 sec

Week 12 (Deload or taper)
- If client responds well, use a deload: 50–60% weights, 2–3 sets per exercise, 8–12 reps, reduced volume
- Optional test week: re-test 1RM on squat, bench, and deadlift if desired

Exercise selection notes
- Prioritize: squat patterns (back/front), hip hinge (deadlift/ RDL), push (bench/overhead press), pull (row/ pull-up), accessory work for arms, core, and posterior chain.
- Replacements by equipment:
  - If no rack: goblet squat, trap bar deadlift, DB bench, DB row, push-ups
  - If no leg curl: glute bridge with band, Nordic hamstring slide
  - If no lat pull: inverted rows, resistance band pulldowns
- Tempo guidance: 2–0–2 (2 seconds lowering, 0 pause, 2 seconds lifting) for hypertrophy sets; 1–0–1 for strength sets.

Volume, intensity, and progression guidelines
- Intro baseline: 3–4 sets per main lift, 5–6 reps per set for strength emphasis and 8–12 for hypertrophy on accessory lifts
- Progressive overload: aim to add 2.5–5% loads every 1–2 weeks where form remains solid; if not possible, add reps within target range or add one accessory set
- Autoregulation: adjust intensities via RPE scale; if fatigue high, reduce sets or load 5–10% and maintain technique

Rest and recovery
- Rest between sets: 2–4 minutes on main compound lifts; 60–90 seconds on accessory lifts
- Sleep: 7–9 hours per night
- Recovery: light cardio and mobility on rest days; minimum 1 day fully off per week
- Mobility: 5–10 minutes of dynamic warm-up pre-workout, 5–10 minutes of static or mobility work post-workout

Nutrition and body composition guidance
- Macros: use a moderate protein target (1.6–2.2 g/kg body weight per day). 
  - Example: for a 60 kg person, 96–132 g of protein/day
- Calories: start at maintenance or slight surplus (100–300 kcal/day) for growth; if fat loss is preferred, maintain a slight deficit (−250 kcal/day) with sufficient protein
- Hydration: 2–3 L per day, adjust for body size and activity
- Pre-workout fueling: balanced meal with protein and carbs 1–2 hours before lifting; post-workout protein within 60–90 minutes
- Nutrient timing: not essential for everyone, but helps for performance; emphasize protein distribution across meals

Tracking and progression
- Weekly check-ins: body weight, workouts completed, RPE, any pain or discomfort
- Progress photos and measurements (waist, hips, and limb circumferences) every 4 weeks if identity tracked
- Adjustments: modify volume or intensity if fatigue or soreness is significant or if technique breaks down

Safety and contraindications
- Maintain proper form on all lifts; stop if pain (not normal muscle fatigue) occurs
- If any cycle-related concerns arise unexpectedly, reassess with the client

Sample weekly schedule (example)
- Monday: Lower Day A
- Tuesday: Upper Day A
- Thursday: Lower Day B
- Friday: Upper Day B
- Optional accessory day or light cardio on off days if client desires

Progress checks and deloads
- If client completes weeks 1–3 with steady progress and low fatigue, continue
- Implement a deload in Week 11–12 or Week 12 depending on fatigue and performance

Note on cycle and contraception
- Since the client is on a combined oral contraceptive with minimal withdrawal symptoms, use general fatigue management. No cycle-related adjustments are necessary unless symptoms change.
- If client experiences significant PMS or performance issues, consider strategic adjustments in volume or nutrition, or a temporary deload.

If you’d like, I can tailor this plan to her exact equipment (barbell availability, machine access, etc.), bodyweight, and lift preferences, and provide a week-by-week day-by-day sheet with exact exercises, sets, and reps for Weeks 1–12.
